local_checks.invariant: No attacker-controlled value (branch name, input, matrix value, artifact name, step output) is expanded by ${{ }} inside a run: script; every third-party action is pinned by a 40-hex commit SHA.
local_checks.result: A scan of every run: block in the three workflows found 0 ${{ }} expressions inside scripts; all values reach scripts via env: (inputs.from-source, inputs.release-tier, step outputs, matrix.shard). All uses: are SHA-pinned (checkout, setup-uv, cache restore/save, upload/download-artifact, attest, codecov, gh-action-pypi-publish, configure/deploy/upload-pages). Saved as evidence/expression_scan.txt.

local_checks.invariant: Every job that reads, judges, signs or publishes the release assets reads exactly the bytes the build job produced, bound by immutable artifact id and digest, never by name.
local_checks.result: same-bytes, save-set, judge-macos/linux/windows/release, coverage, verify, attest, publish and pypi each refuse an empty or non-numeric assets-id (an empty id would fetch every artifact), download by artifact-ids with digest-mismatch: error, check SHA256SUMS against the 64-hex sums-sha256 the build handed on, check every file against SHA256SUMS, and require no other file (release.yml:380-415, 2440-2475, 2506-2541, 2564-2599). attest signs release-assets/* from that verified folder and re-verifies with --signer-workflow release.yml@$GITHUB_REF, --source-ref and --deny-self-hosted-runners (2476-2487); publish uploads the same folder with --verify-tag; pypi takes the wheel from the same folder. Rebuild votes come from separate jobs (not a matrix), so one leg cannot cast both votes.

local_checks.invariant: A cached set (written by a branch run, by set-cache on main, or by a release.yml dispatch on main) never reaches a tag's signature or publication, and a reused set cannot yield a green run unless two in-run rebuilds from the pins give the same bytes.
local_checks.result: Reuse is decided only for workflow_dispatch on a branch other than refs/heads/main with from-source false and an exact-key hit (release.yml:79-91); no restore-keys prefix matching. A tag run's only cache contact is lookup-only (no download or extraction). gather.py G7 also refuses a tag whose set-source is not 'built' (gather.py:381-382). On a reuse run, set_key.py verify checks every file against the set's own SHA256SUMS, no extra file, MANIFEST pin/recipe lines against the checkout and the key (set_key.py:164-208); that is self-consistency only, and the independent binding is same-bytes: both rebuild jobs' SHA256SUMS must equal the set's byte for byte and the wheel must equal both rebuilt wheels byte for byte (release.yml:448-488), and gather needs same-bytes. Observed cache scopes (evidence/gh_caches.json) are refs/heads/main and spec/wave branches only; fork pull_request runs (docs.yml only) write only refs/pull/N/merge, which no branch or main run reads.

local_checks.invariant: same-bytes binds the published .tar.xz's inner files to the two rebuilds.
local_checks.result: Dummy-fixture replay of the same-bytes step (release.yml:448-457): a tarball holding the genuine SHA256SUMS but a substituted python.wasm passes both cmp checks with exit 0; the step never runs the inner files against the inner SHA256SUMS. The gap is closed downstream, not here: the judge legs point WASI_PYTHON_ARTIFACTS at that extracted tarball and the runner checks MANIFEST, the binary and the stdlib zip against the set's SHA256SUMS before use (src/wasi_python/_artifacts.py _found_and_checked), so a mismatched tarball turns the judges and gather red; the wheel's artifacts are checked against the sums and against both rebuilt wheels. Recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Only a v* release tag on main's history can sign, publish a GitHub release, publish to PyPI or deploy Pages; dispatches and pull requests never do.
local_checks.result: Top-level permissions: {} in all three workflows; per-job grants are contents: read except attest (id-token, attestations write), publish (contents write, environment release), pypi (id-token, environment pypi, vars.PYPI_PUBLISH) and docs deploy (pages, id-token, environment github-pages). attest/publish/pypi require event push and ref_type tag; build checks version.py check --tag (tag == v<__version__>, changelog dated) and git merge-base --is-ancestor GITHUB_SHA origin/main with fetch-depth 0 under bash -e (release.yml:135-143). Hosted facts observed by read-only gh GET: environments release and pypi allow only tag pattern v*, github-pages allows main and v* (evidence/gh_env_branch_policies.json); ruleset 'release tags are protected' blocks creation/update/deletion of refs/tags/v* and 'main is protected' blocks update/non-fast-forward/deletion of main, bypass only for the admin role (evidence/gh_ruleset_details.json); the only collaborator is the admin owner (evidence/gh_collaborators.json); default workflow token is read; fork PRs need approval for first-time contributors. Releases are immutable (v0.1.0 immutable: true). The v0.1.0 run 39957192055 was a tag push by the owner and every gate job succeeded before attest, publish and pypi. docs.yml deploy on a dispatch from a non-main branch is refused by the github-pages branch policy; pull_request runs build only, with contents: read and no secrets.

local_checks.invariant: The attestation identity the workflow signs and the policy users are told to verify agree and pin workflow, ref and runner.
local_checks.result: The v0.1.0 SLSA provenance (read via gh api .../attestations, evidence/attestation_identity_v0.1.0.txt) names https://github.com/ClayGendron/wasi_python/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v0.1.0, event push, commit 2cd47507, github-hosted, matching the release notes' command (version.py:295-306). The repository has since been renamed to ClayGendron/wasi-python (evidence/gh_repo.json) while version.py:301-303 and docs/how-to/verify-a-download.md:20-21 still hard-code ClayGendron/wasi_python; the workflow's own check uses $GITHUB_REPOSITORY. This fails closed (the old name is in the owner's own namespace and cannot be claimed by another account), so it is hardening, not a forgery path.

local_checks.invariant: Failure, cancellation, skipped or missing shard outputs never let gather, attest or publish proceed.
local_checks.result: gather runs under !cancelled() && !failure() but refuses any empty or non-numeric record id and any non-64-hex sha (release.yml:1765-1784, 2037-2042; gather.py G1), fails a tag or main run whose TIER is not release (gather.py:141-142), and binds python.wasm and the set's SHA256SUMS to the lane's accepted history (G7). attest and publish have no status function, so they need every need to succeed; pypi needs publish. Upstream kits fetched in judge legs are verified by SHA-256 (fetch.py:73-88).

hardening: Release authorization rests on one identity: both rulesets give the admin role bypass_mode 'always', the only collaborator is that admin, and the release, pypi and github-pages environments have a branch/tag policy but no required reviewer. The tag-on-main check (release.yml:140) lives in the tagged commit's own workflow file, so it binds only an unmodified release.yml. Any process holding the owner's token (local automation included) can create a v* tag on a non-main commit with an edited release.yml and get an attestation, an immutable GitHub release and a PyPI upload with no second check. Fix: add a required reviewer to the release and pypi environments, put attest in the release environment so id-token is issued only after that gate, and limit ruleset bypass for refs/tags/v* creation to an explicit actor, not 'always' for the admin role.

Stale signing identity in what users are told to run: release/version.py:301-303 (which writes the GitHub release notes) and docs/how-to/verify-a-download.md:20-21 hard-code --repo/--signer-workflow ClayGendron/wasi_python. The repository is now ClayGendron/wasi-python, so the next release's attestation will carry the new name and every user's documented gh attestation verify will fail, while the attest job's own check (release.yml:2484-2486, using $GITHUB_REPOSITORY) passes. This fails closed but invites users to drop the policy. Fix: build the note from GITHUB_REPOSITORY, and have the attest job run the exact command printed in notes.md.

same-bytes (release.yml:448-457) compares only the tarball's inner SHA256SUMS with the rebuilds. It never checks the inner files against that file (local dummy replay: evidence same_bytes_fixture.log). Today the judge legs' runner integrity check closes this for MANIFEST, the binaries and the stdlib zip, but not for the licence files. Fix: add (cd set/wasi-python-* && sha256sum --strict -c SHA256SUMS) and a listed-equals-present check to same-bytes, as the wheel step already does.

Main-scope set caches are written by set-cache.yml's seed job (no in-run rebuild proof) and by release.yml's save-set on a main dispatch. actions/cache restore extracts with tar -P, so code running in any main-ref job (for example the Codecov uploader, fetched by version name at run time in the coverage job on a main dispatch) could plant an entry under a predictable key that later runs code in a branch reuse run's build job. Today that ends red: same-bytes, the wheel comparison and the judges' runner check all apply, and branch runs never sign or publish. The worst case is false-red or denial of branch dry runs. Fix: restrict cache writes to set-cache, and consider dropping save-set on main.

PyPI trusted-publisher scope cannot be seen from here. Observed: PYPI_PUBLISH=true, and the pypi job published 0.1.0. The pypi environment's v* policy holds only if PyPI's trusted publisher for wasi-python requires environment 'pypi'. Without that, a release.yml run on any ref whose job drops the environment line could mint a PyPI token (only the admin can push today). Owner check: on pypi.org > wasi-python > Publishing, confirm the GitHub publisher names workflow release.yml and environment pypi.

The verify job installs the wheel with uv run --isolated --no-project --with, which resolves wasmtime from PyPI at run time with no lock or hashes. That matches what users get, and the job only gates attest; it cannot change the assets.

Same effect as the documented dict/set item (quadratic CPU until the deadline); docs/explanation/security-model.md:101 could name XML parsing alongside dict and set keys.

_zip._member_parts (src/wasi_python/_zip.py:108-119) does not refuse Windows-reserved names (CON, NUL, COM1...), components ending in a dot or space, or names equal under case folding; the shipped inner archive holds none (checked), and its input is the checked set, so this matters only for a caller-supplied artifacts= set. Refusing them would make the guard hold on its own.

Both binaries keep 31 assert __FILE__ strings and the zip four build-config modules under the fixed container prefix /wasi-python-build/; no user or host identity, but -ffile-prefix-map (and the host_neutral rewrite already used for _sysconfigdata) could drop them.

reactor_main.c starts with pinned=1, so the load-time constructors (mimalloc and wasi-libc state) of the plain binary, not only the snapshot, see zeroed entropy; guest code always sees real entropy (checked). Inside-guest allocator randomness is not a host boundary; note only.
The br_table maximum (3,203 labels against ~256k for GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm) is measured by hand; a per-build check would keep it true until the runner moves to wasmtime-py 49.0.4 or later.

Locally, build/artifacts/python-stdlib.zip has link count 5: research work trees under build/ (output-capture-costs, rust-spike-perf, scratch-wt50, concurrency-probe) hard-link it as lib/python315.zip. Developer environment only; the runner re-hashes the zip before each copy, so a write through one of those links would be refused, not used.

If pkg-config ever failed to find step 37's sheenbidi.pc, meson would git-clone SheenBidi master over the network and build it into the plot libraries. The zero-patch judge (tests/harness/pins.py, 'files the build adds are not judged') would not flag the added subprojects/sheenbidi folder. The recorded build resolved every dependency through pkg-config, so this is hardening. Fix: add `--wrap-mode=nodownload` (or wrap_mode = 'nodownload' under [built-in options] in each recipes/*.cross), and have the judge flag any subprojects/ entry a tree did not ship.

scripts/assemble_artifacts.py checks some downloads it reads with pinned_bytes() (tqdm, reportlab, the MPL and MIT texts). It reads others without that check: wheel_licences(d / wheel) for each WHEELS entry, the sympy wheel's nested licence, the wasi-libc and LLVM notices, and the Unicode terms. All of these become release LICENSES files. 00_download.sh verified them earlier in a full build, but a step run alone (build.sh can run from a named step) skips that. scripts/00_download.sh's curl has no --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https', so a redirect could leave HTTPS. That fails closed, but a poisoned downloads cache would cause a lasting red build.

pyproject.toml's [build-system] requires = ["hatchling"] is unbounded. The release builds use the hashed release/build-constraints.txt, and no sdist is published. A build without the constraints, local or downstream, resolves the newest hatchling.

When a guest buffer crosses the end of memory, or `used` is out of bounds, wasmtime 49.0.0 writes whole entries (their padding from uninitialized host memory) and then traps. The guard runs only on errno 0, so nothing zeroes those entries. _shared then records the stop and returns EIO. The guest stops at its next function entry or loop header, so python.wasm cannot read the bytes. A hand-written wasm guest could read and fd_write them in straight-line code before that check: wasmtime's own fd_write is not shadowed and does not consult call.stopped. A crafted guest is outside the project's stated threat model, and the padding read zero on this host. _zeroed grows the stat trampoline's private page up to the guest memory's size. The store limiter's memory_size applies to each linear memory, so this second memory is bounded by memory_bytes on its own, not jointly with the guest's. Pages are reserved lazily and only the listing's bytes are touched, so resident growth equals the listing, which wasmtime already holds on the host. Joint accounting would make memory_bytes a whole-store bound.

PreparedCall.call assigns into ctypes c_int32/c_int64 union fields, which truncate out-of-range Python ints silently. Every computed forward argument is below 2**32 today. hardening: Fork refusal keys off wasi_python's own engine only (_engines._engine sets fork_used). When a parent compiled any module through wasmtime-py directly, a forked child's run() hangs for good inside wasmtime_module_new waiting on the parent's rayon compile pool (observed: fork_foreign.log, fork_foreign_sample.txt). The hang comes before the guest runs, so no deadline or Ctrl-C ends it. The fork is the embedder's own act and no guest can cause it, so this is not a finding. Document it, or refuse a child whenever the parent had made a wasmtime Engine.

_write_output copies the whole write with ctypes.string_at before _Stream.write applies the cap, so a guest past its output limit still costs one host copy per write, as large as the write. Copying only the room left would make the cap bound this work too.

wasmtime-py's LAST_EXCEPTION slot is process-wide. The runner's host functions never raise into it, so a process that runs only wasi_python is unaffected. But if the embedder's own wasmtime-py host function raises at the same time as a wasi_python guest traps, the runner's Func.__call__ paths (the run export, _initialize, host_alloc) can pick up that foreign exception and raise it from run(). This is upstream's design.

The Linux trap-handler check runs before each entry, not during a call. If a tool, host or provider replaces wasmtime's SIGSEGV or SIGILL handler during a call (for example with faulthandler.enable()), a guest trap later in that same call ends the process. The guest can choose when to trap, for example with an out-of-bounds read through numpy as_strided. Re-checking in the epoch callback or after each hand-off home would close the window.

_wasmtime_ffi.check verifies only that the private names exist, plus the arity of two binding records. A version-equality warning, or a behavioural self-test at import, would catch a 49.x patch that changes one of these.

local_checks.invariant: _resolve: a mount path is relative, NUL-free, components at most 255 bytes, never climbs above the descriptor's folder even momentarily, and never names a more specific preopen's path
local_checks.result: _resolve (_fs_paths.py:63-91) refuses absolute (EPERM), NUL (EINVAL), long components (ENAMETOOLONG), any '..' at or below the floor (EPERM), and resolved paths equal to or under base.mount.nested (EPERM); raw paths are capped at MAX_PATH and decoded as UTF-8 before (_fs_memory.py:267-282). Nested preopens are computed per mount from every other preopen and mount guest path, including /usr/local/lib for a mount at '/' (_fs_table.py:100-114). Backslash, ':' and device names pass through by design and are documented (docs/how-to/mounts.md).

local_checks.invariant: Read-only mounts never reach the write half; writable mounts' namespace calls keep the guest's view of nested preopens and never cross into wasmtime places
local_checks.result: Writes decided before any provider call: _path_open EPERM on a read-only mount when CREAT/TRUNC/FD_WRITE (138-140), _namespace EPERM (370-371), set_times/_refused EPERM, fd_write/pwrite/set_size check entry.writable and mount.writable. Renames: '/' or names ending '.'/'..' EBUSY, src/dst above a nested preopen EBUSY (_above), into own subfolder EINVAL; rename/link across a mount and any other descriptor go to _across, which answers EPERM or EXDEV without forwarding a rename or link; fd_renumber onto or from a table number is ENOTSUP. A closed mount preopen falls back to wasmtime's empty read-only placeholder under the call's 0700 private folder.

local_checks.invariant: Provider answers are typed before use, run on the home thread behind the gate, and staged within bounds; write-backs follow renames and skip unlinked or removed paths
local_checks.result: _stat_answer/_read_answer/_list_answer judge exact types, cap staged bytes, refuse listed names that are empty, dots, contain '/' or NUL, exceed 255 bytes or repeat (_listed); every provider step runs through _home after _gate (cancel, deadline, file-call limit). _follow moves open descriptors with a successful rename and unlinks those at a removed or replaced dst, so an end-of-call write-back goes to the file's current path and never to a nested preopen (dst under nested is refused by _resolve).

local_checks.invariant: A hostile guest cannot climb out of a mount, reach a nested grant through the mount's descriptor, write a read-only mount, or rename from a mount into a grant; the provider sees only normalized in-mount paths
local_checks.result: With a read-only Mount at /m and a read-only Grant at /m/g: '/m/../m/a.txt', '/m/d/../../x', dir_fd '../a.txt' all EPERM; '/m/d/../g/secret.txt' (the grant spelled past wasi-libc through the mount) EPERM while '/m/g/secret.txt' reads the grant; append to /m/a.txt EPERM; mkdir EPERM; rename /m -> /m/g EPERM. The provider saw only read '/a.txt', list '/d' and the documented backslash name '/..\..\x'. Run with lane.lock absent, wrapped in ulimit -t 300 -f 4000000 -n 4096, env -i (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, WASI_PYTHON_CACHE under scratch), sandbox-exec deny network*, .venv/bin/python -I, wasmtime-py 49.0.0 on darwin arm64, the local build/artifacts set; fixtures and every grant only under scratch/fx; the target was not mounted read-only (not enforceable on this platform).

hardening: docs/explanation/security-model.md:20 says the runner refuses 'a grant or root over any module cache it knows of', but _judge (src/wasi_python/_places.py:351-362) checks runtime folders against writable places only; a read-only grant over the module cache is accepted (executed). Either judge every grant against the caches or narrow the sentence to writable grants, as docs/how-to/grants.md:104 already says.

make_missing (src/wasi_python/_platform.py:387-409) treats FileExistsError as 'a concurrent call made it' and adopts the folder, and mkdir uses the umask's mode: a missing root named in a folder another OS user can write (for example /tmp on Linux) can be pre-created and owned by that user, who can then read and plant data in a root the embedder expected to be fresh. Making the missing components 0700 and refusing a made component not owned by this user (fstat st_uid) closes it; today the embedder's choice of path is the only control.

_runtime_folders (src/wasi_python/_places.py:526-573) protects sysconfig's stdlib/purelib/platlib/scripts, the user site, wasi_python and wasmtime-py, but not other host sys.path entries (PYTHONPATH, .pth-added editable sources); a writable grant over those is accepted and a guest could plant modules the host imports later. Embedder-chosen, so not a finding; judging every existing sys.path folder would extend the existing rule.

path_filestat_set_times and fd_filestat_set_times stay wasmtime 49.0.0's own on calls without mounts and are forwarded unchanged with mounts; GHSA-j2g9-4prp-pf6h (host panic on an out-of-range time, fixed in 49.0.1) is in range. The project's own test found CPython's utime never passes a triggering value, so it needs a crafted raw call; the existing guard machinery could clamp or refuse out-of-range times for defence in depth.

A mount's resolved path is built from the descriptor's own path plus up to MAX_PATH bytes, so nested opens through folder descriptors can hand a provider paths longer than 4,096 bytes; harmless to the boundary, but a cap on the resolved length would keep provider work bounded the same way.
